findings.title: Backup codes can be redeemed concurrently more than once
findings.body: Two login requests can both read the same stored backup-code list, find the supplied code, and then each write a copy with that slot set to null. Since the updates do not compare against the original stored value, both requests succeed and create sessions, violating the one-use guarantee. Make consumption atomic so only one request can update the list and authenticate.

findings.title: Federated 2FA users cannot choose the backup-code flow
findings.body: The Lost access control is added only to `TwoFactorFooter`. When `totpEmail` is present—which is how federated-login users are sent to the 2FA prompt—the page uses `ExternalTotpFooter`, which has no Lost access action. These users therefore have no UI path to enter a backup code.

findings.title: Backup-code-only credentials are rejected for federated users
findings.body: The new backup-code branch below this check accepts `backupCode`, but the earlier identity-provider guards require `credentials.totpCode`. A backup-code submission has no TOTP code, so federated users are rejected with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` before backup-code verification runs. Update the guards to recognize backup-code credentials as an allowed second factor.

findings.title: The password visibility toggle cannot reveal this password
findings.body: This field is now a `PasswordField`, but it still passes `type="password"`. `PasswordField` spreads caller props after its visibility-controlled `type`, so this prop overrides the toggle and the input remains masked even after clicking the eye button.

findings.title: Password visibility controls are no longer keyboard-accessible
findings.body: Setting the show/hide button to `tabIndex={-1}` removes it from normal keyboard tab navigation. Keyboard-only users cannot reach the control to reveal or hide a password; keep it in the tab order.

findings.title: The tests do not exercise backup-code authentication
findings.body: The added test checks the download filename and that a toast appears, but never submits a generated backup code to log in or verifies that the code is rejected after use. The central authentication behavior and its one-time guarantee can therefore regress without any test failure; add coverage for backup-code login and reuse.
